title: Consumption telemetry handoff and fallback orchestration for billing pipelines
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Streaming inference traffic can generate partial and out-of-order consumption events (stream fragments, retries, and multi-model fallbacks). Current downstream billing consumers expect compact, idempotent consumption records. This ticket builds a handoff orchestration layer that normalizes streaming telemetry into durable consumption records, provides graceful fallback when the primary aggregator is unavailable, and emits signals for downstream billing and analytics with clear delivery semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Handoff service accepts per-request streaming telemetry and emits a single canonical consumption record per user request within 10s under normal load
When aggregator is unavailable, fallback sampling mode emits lightweight summaries that preserve >=95% of cost-weighted signal for top 10% customers
All emitted records are idempotent (using consumption_id) and can be compacted by the billing job without double-charges
End-to-end tests demonstrate no loss of billing revenue in a 7-day rolling window compared to current production baseline (within 0.5%)
Tracing and metrics added: ingest_latency_p50/p95, handoff_fallback_rate, duplicate_emitted_count, downstream_ack_lag
design_decisions: Create a lightweight ingestion shim colocated with streaming gateway to convert fragments into staged events
Use a monotonic consumption_id derived from request_id + sequence to enable idempotency and cheap sampling
Primary path writes full consumption records to durable Kafka topic with tombstone semantics; fallback path writes aggregated summaries to a cold-topics with TTL
Downstream billing consumer reads canonical topic and performs final compaction in a windowed consumer; we do not attempt synchronous billing in the handoff layer
Expose a small HTTP control plane to toggle fallback sampling thresholds and grace periods without restart
migration_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy handoff shim to 5% of gateway pods in us-west-2, dual-write canonical topic and mirror to legacy pipeline
Phase 2: enable compaction consumer in read-only mode and compare outputs against legacy pipeline for 48h
Phase 3: if divergence <0.5% and no critical errors, promote to 50% traffic and monitor metrics for 72h
Phase 4: full rollout and decommission legacy intermediate accumulator after 7-day verification window
risks: Mis-aggregation during retries could undercount or overcount if idempotency keys are malformed
Fallback sampling could bias small customers if sampling thresholds are not tuned by cost-weighted signal
Kafka hot-partitioning risk — need key selection strategy to avoid per-customer skew
Operational complexity: more topics and TTL semantics increase maintenance burden for SRE
tests: Unit tests for consumption_id derivation and idempotency behavior
Integration test that replays production capture (1h sample) through shim and verifies billing consumer output equals baseline
Chaos test: kill aggregator and verify fallback summaries preserve top-10 revenue footprint
Load test: sustained 10k rps canonicalization with p95 ingest latency <200ms
rollout_steps: Create feature flag in console to opt customers into new handoff (feature: consumption_handoff_v1)
Deploy shim as sidecar to gateway Canary cluster and enable dual-write
Run comparison job and collect divergence dashboard (dashboard link in comments)
Incrementally increase traffic and monitor the compaction consumer and billing totals
Switch default to canonical topic once verified and disable legacy mirror
